subject: Reserved capacity proposal for CloudMetrics — conditional price protection
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Zhao <lina@cloudmetrics.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity proposal for CloudMetrics — conditional price protection

Hi Lina,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — excited by the fit between CloudMetrics' realtime inference needs and Redwood Dedicated. I've attached a sizing workbook (capacity_model_v2.xlsx) and a draft term sheet (redwood-dedicated-term-draft.docx) for the 18-month reserved capacity we discussed.

Two asks upfront so we can turn this into a mutual action plan:
- Can your procurement team confirm target start month (Oct vs Nov) for billing ramp?
- Are you open to a conditional pricing protection clause (outlined in the draft) that adjusts the effective discount if our underlying GPU index moves beyond agreed bands? It protects both sides vs large market moves.

Proposal highlights (high-level):
- Reserved SKU: 12 x A100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated pool)
- Commitment: 18 months, baseline throughput 5k tokens/s (burst to 10k)
- Base discount: 28% off list for the term; conditional step-down floor at 18% if market GPU index rises > 22% relative to baseline for two consecutive months
- Routing option: Redwood can temporarily route workloads to near-term compatible SKUs (quantized variants or preemptible pools) under defined latency caps if capacity constraints occur; would require a <24hr notice and transparency to metrics.

I've called out the conditional step-down as a compromise: it gives you predictable savings now while limiting Redwood's exposure if raw GPU costs spike. If you'd like a firm cap rather than a step-down, we can surface a limited one-time market surcharge credit instead (we can discuss specifics).

Please loop in procurement and legal if the draft looks roughly aligned and tell me any non-starters. Happy to jump on a call this week to walk the mechanics.

Best,
Sergio
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Lina Zhao <lina@cloudmetrics.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@cloudmetrics.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity proposal for CloudMetrics — conditional price protection

Sergio,

Thanks for the deck and the draft. A few quick clarifications from procurement's side:

- The step-down is okay in principle, but we need a clear, auditable GPU index and a hard cap on the total discount erosion over the term. Our CFO won't accept an open-ended ratchet.
- If you route to alternative SKUs during a spike, what's the SLA impact? We need a latency SLO (p95) guarantee or a credit mechanism.
- Can you confirm billing start: earliest Nov 1 — we need 30 days to provision network peering and KMS configuration.

I'll also need a list of the observable metrics that will be available in the Console for audit.

Looping in procurement — can someone from Redwood supply the index spec and the monitoring/metrics commitment?

Thanks,
Lina Zhao
Head of Engineering, CloudMetrics
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 13:00:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Reserved capacity proposal for CloudMetrics — conditional price protection

Team — forwarding CloudMetrics' procurement asks. Short background: CloudMetrics is scaled realtime telemetry; fairly sensitive to p95 latency. They want a firm cap on how much the discount can be reduced via the GPU index clause and SLO-level commitments if we use alternative SKUs (quantized variants/preemptible).

Why this is different:
- The deal is large (DEAL-8421-CLM) and strategic; they want reserve-by-department footprints across three product lines in Q1.
- Market exposure if GPU prices spike could materially impact margins for the term if we offer the full base discount and then have a large index-driven erosion.

Suggested ask for approval:
- Allow the conditional step-down, but cap total discount erosion at 8 percentage points across the term (i.e., base 28% min floor 20% not lower) — this gives them predictability and protects our economics.
- Require we publish the GPU index spec (we use a weighted market spot index + supplier PSU pricing) and agree to monthly publication in the Console (read-only view for customer).
- If routing to alternative SKUs, guarantee p95 latency within 20% of baseline or provide a service credit (0.5% of monthly fee per SLA miss, capped at 5%).
- One-time credit: if CloudMetrics defers start past Nov 1 due to procurement, offer a 10% onboarding credit in month 1.

Attachments: capacity_model_v2.xlsx (sizing scenarios for various routing mixes).

Can finance/FP&A (Marcus) confirm whether the 8pp cap is ok from a margin perspective and if Exec Sales (Marissa) can sign off on an exception for this account. If we need Legal to tighten wording around "routing" vs "reallocation" we should create a short SOW addendum.

— Sergio
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity proposal for CloudMetrics — conditional price protection

Sergio — good summary. Approve in principle with the following constraints:

1) Cap discount erosion at 8pp (base 28% -> floor 20%) — approved.
2) GPU index spec: product must coordinate with Research to publish the index algorithm; legal to review nomenclature so it is auditable.
3) SLA/credit: approve the p95 latency guardrail within 20% and the credit scheme as outlined, but cap total monthly credits at 10% of the monthly invoice.
4) Onboarding credit: approve the 10% one-time credit if start is delayed past Nov 1, but the credit must be repaid if they terminate within 90 days.

Next steps: Legal (Rachel) — please draft the redlines to the term sheet to reflect the cap, index publication, and routing SOW. Marcus — confirm margin sensitivity against the 20% floor and provide a quick P&L delta. Ben — coordinate a single call (with procurement and engineering) to walk the index and Console monitoring.

We should avoid setting a precedent that broadly guarantees fixed GPU caps to customers; treat this as a one-off for strategic accounts but document the approval path. Once legal has the redline, Sergio please return the updated draft to Lina and procurement.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
